sections.overview: This large minnow is native to western North America, including the Columbia River and its tributaries.
sections.identification: It has a long snout and large mouth, a greenish back and sides, a pale belly and opaque fins.
sections.habitat: It occurs in the Columbia and Snake rivers and in lakes and streams across the region.
sections.diet: Larger fish are opportunistic predators of aquatic invertebrates and fishes, including young salmon and steelhead.
sections.behavior: It is a well-studied native predator in the Columbia and Snake river systems.
sections.reproduction: The consulted species summaries did not provide reproductive details.
sections.ecology: Its predation on juvenile salmonids has prompted research and management programs, without implying that the native fish should be eradicated.
sections.conservation: No global conservation category was given in the consulted accounts.
